hook_text: When the Dutch arrived at the Cape in 1652, they were not the first people there. Not even close.
clip_script: For tens of thousands of years, San hunter-gatherers lived across southern Africa, tracking eland, gathering roots and berries, and painting their world on rock walls. For about two thousand years, Khoikhoi herders had grazed fat-tailed sheep and long-horned cattle along the coast, moving with the seasons, packing their reed-mat homes onto oxen. They traded with passing ships for copper and beads. Then, in 1652, the Dutch East India Company built a fort, and everything began to change. This term, we tell that story from more than one side.
visual_style: Rock art of eland fades into a coastal scene of cattle and reed huts; a sailing ship appears on the horizon of Table Bay.
pacing: Slow and spacious, with a turn at the ship.
